A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLM-ITL and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The existing material can be matched across versions, including relocated figures; v3 adds Appendix I. No material gaps limit comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original topic-coherence and document-alignment experiments on four corpora, together with ablations, sensitivity analyses and prompt experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds an alignment-loss ablation in Table 3 and word-vector evaluation results in Table I1.

M1.justification: The proposed topic-suggestion procedure, confidence weighting, OT alignment and warm-up objective remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 1. Alternative losses are evaluated as ablation variants rather than adopted into the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use 20News, R8, DBpedia and AGNews for the same topic-modeling and document-representation tasks. The added evaluations reuse this coverage without introducing new populations, domains or input scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 3 newly evaluates KL divergence, Jensen–Shannon divergence, Hellinger distance and Total Variation distance as alternatives to OT alignment. The main topic-model baselines and existing confidence and prompt comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds an alternative-alignment-distance ablation using ETM on 20News with K=50, plus W2V-Cosine, W2V-L1 and W2V-L2 evaluation in Appendix I. Previously reported splits, preprocessing, training settings and CV/PN evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Table 3 ablation tests whether OT is preferable to four other distribution measures for topic refinement. This is a focused addition on one dataset and base model; existing warm-up, confidence, LLM, hyperparameter and prompt studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five differently seeded runs with mean and standard-deviation reporting, except TopicGPT, which is run once at zero temperature in Appendix D.2. The new tables follow the existing uncertainty-reporting convention.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds alternative-loss results: CV is 0.479–0.480 versus the retained OT result of 0.578, while PN is 0.402–0.405 versus OT's 0.398. Table I1 adds word-vector scores, including 20News W2V-Cosine of 0.218 for ETM and 0.177 with LLM-ITL. Existing benchmark scores and plotted results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions and Equations (1)–(11) remain equivalent. The added empirical comparisons introduce no new formal definitions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about improving topic interpretability while maintaining document representations, computational efficiency and flexibility across NTMs and LLMs.

C2.justification: Appendix I adds a human-relevance rationale for evaluation, citing closer agreement of word-vector metrics with human judgments than standard coherence metrics. Existing explanations of corpus bias, warm-up tradeoffs and the Section 7 limitation are retained.

D1.justification: v2 promises that code and datasets will be available at Github; v3 supplies a specific repository link and states that they are available. This improves access documentation, although actual repository availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds background citations on hierarchical Bayesian topic models and OT applications, cites Nikolenko (2016) for word-vector evaluation, and replaces the ChatGPT reference with the GPT-4 technical report. The central positioning against document-level LLM methods and post-hoc refinement remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include brief background expansions, reordering the qualitative and warm-up discussions, wording and bibliography edits, corresponding-author notes and an acknowledgment. Most existing prose and the overall section structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 3 and I1 and moves v2's prompt illustration from Figure A1 into the main text as Figure 2. Existing figure graphics are unchanged, with associated renumbering, appendix rearrangement and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The added OT ablation supplies direct evidence for an important design choice, while Appendix I checks coherence gains using additional semantic measures. Explicit code/data access information also improves reproducibility documentation. These are focused gains: the added evaluations use ETM, and Table 3 supports an OT coherence advantage while reporting slightly lower alignment scores than the alternatives.
